title: Forecasting fallback-ready model inventory and procurement triggers
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Objective: produce a prioritized, forecastable inventory of candidate model variants (open and partner-supplied) that are 'fallback-ready' for Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Deliverables: 1) a scoring rubric for fallback readiness (availability, latency delta, quantization compatibility, license risk, integration effort), 2) a live sheet with prioritized models + procurement trigger rules, 3) a short playbook for on-call and sales that maps triggers to actions. Motivation: unpredictable upstream model availability and provider pricing spikes have caused 2 customer incidents in the last 6 months; we need systematic signals and procurement/rollout responses to keep customer-facing SLAs intact.
comments: 2025-02-10 Sofia Alvarez: Kickoff — scoped with Platform and Sales. Agreed success metric: reduce customer-visible fallback activations requiring manual intervention from 3/month to 0-1/month within Q2.

2025-02-12 Arjun Patel: Spoke with Runtime team (ENG). They can reliably deploy & test 3 candidate variants per week for compatibility but need a prioritized queue and model artifacts (repo links + quantization guidance). Asked for kernel/quantization compatibility matrix from Research.

2025-02-13 Research note (Anika): preliminary scan of 12 open models. Observations: 4 are quantization-amenable with minimal accuracy loss; 2 have restrictive licenses; 3 show high latency variability on smaller GPUs. Added baseline metrics to the workshop sheet.

2025-02-15 PM review: Drafted scoring rubric and weights. Shared with Design and Solutions for feedback (link below). Design requested clear UI fields for Console to surface fallback tier and reason codes.

2025-02-17 Sales feedback (thread #fallback-playbook): prefer triggers tied to committed capacity thresholds and price-per-token anomalies; suggested adding customer tier mapping so enterprise customers get earlier notifications.
2025-02-18 Engineering (ENG-23109) update: hooking up an instrument that exports model availability and price spikes to the central Signal Hub. ETA for initial feed: 2025-02-27.

2025-02-20 Sofia: Updated rubric after Research accuracy validation experiment. Next: finalize trigger thresholds and run a 2-week simulated failover exercise in staging. Assigned to Arjun to coordinate test schedule.
acceptance_criteria: A prioritized inventory (sheet) with at least 10 candidate model variants across 4 providers, each scored with the rubric
Procurement trigger rules defined (quantitative thresholds) and implemented as alerts in Signal Hub
A documented playbook for ops and sales with step-by-step rollback/fallback actions and owner assignments
Staging simulation: at least one automatic fallback test executed with monitoring dashboards capturing latency/cost deltas
tasks: Finalize scoring rubric and weights (availability, latency delta, accuracy drift, integration effort, license risk)
Populate live inventory sheet with metadata + artifact links and baseline measurements
Integrate availability and market price signals into Signal Hub alerts (ENG)
Define procurement triggers and approval flow (Finance + Legal) for fast procurement of partner models
Coordinate 2-week simulated failover in staging and capture metrics (Arjun to schedule)
Produce 1-page playbook for Sales and On-call with runbooks and contact points
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Adopted a weighted scoring rubric vs binary checklist. Weights: availability 30%, latency delta 25%, accuracy risk 20%, integration effort 15%, license risk 10% (temporary — revisit after validation)
2025-02-16: Decided not to include models with 'no-commercial-use' clauses in fallback inventory; flagged as 'research-only' in sheet
2025-02-19: Chose conservative procurement trigger thresholds for enterprise customers (earlier alerts) and aggressive thresholds for self-serve tier; documented rationale in PRD
notes: Measurement plan: capture 7-day rolling median latency and 95th percentile during simulated traffic; compute TCO multiplier (tokens/sec normalized) comparing primary model to fallback
Risk: Some partner SLAs don't permit benchmarking—we will use vendor-provided telemetry and mark those entries with 'external-metrics' tag
Follow-up: schedule Legal review for 'fallback-as-service' contract addendum (possible amendment to Dedicated agreements)
Related artifacts: example Console UI wireframe for 'Fallback Tier' (link in Confluence PRD), draft email templates for customer notification
